title: Can't sync with Proton Drive

comments.author: participant16
comments.body:
I have already forked both henrybear327/proton-api-bridge and henrybear327/go-proton-api, 

The current upload failure has been fixed in my forks.
At the moment, the issue can be resolved by switching rclone to use my forked versions of proton-api-bridge and go-proton-api, without any changes required on the rclone side itself.

Root cause of the upload failures

The previous implementation was missing Proton Drive’s block verification step, which the official web client performs during uploads.

More specifically, each encrypted block must include a per-block verification token, which is derived from:

VerificationCode and ContentKeyPacket returned by the Verification endpoint

a verifier session key decrypted via the file’s node key

a decrypt-check on the encrypted block, followed by an XOR-based token generation

Without this verifier token, the server may initially accept the encrypted block upload, but later reject the block or the revision, resulting in stalled or failed uploads. This matches the behavior users have been reporting.

My fork implements this verification flow to match the official web client behavior, and uploads are now completing successfully in testing.

https://github.com/participant16/rclone/tree/fix-protondrive-upload

comments.author: participant18
comments.body:
@participant13:

**TL;DR:** I took a crack at verifying the current state by successfully uploading an archive to Proton Drive. Currently, uploads are broken without block verification tokens + shouldRetry + draft cleanup. All three fixes exist as open PRs — merging #9080, rclone/go-proton-api#2, and rclone/Proton-API-Bridge#1 should resolve this for everyone.

---
I've been hitting this issue since ~November 2025 (uploads to Proton Drive failing). After investigation, I found three root causes and built/tested a fix across the rclone stack:

Root causes:
1. Proton's storage backend now requires block verification tokens (Verifier.Token in POST /drive/blocks). Without them, every block upload fails with 422 / Code=200501.
2. shouldRetry() in protondrive always returns (false, err), so transient errors are never retried.
3. Failed uploads leave orphaned drafts that cause Code=2500/Code=2501 error loops on retry.

What I tested:
- Built a patched rclone binary (from master) incorporating fixes from PRs #9080, #9081, and rclone/Proton-API-Bridge#1, plus block verification logic ported from ProtonDriveApps/sdk.
- Successfully uploaded a 1.39 GiB Gitea backup to Proton Drive (first successful upload in 4 months).
- Deployed as a Docker image running in production.

Related: rclone/rclone#9080, rclone/rclone#9081, rclone/rclone#9117, rclone/Proton-API-Bridge#1, rclone/go-proton-api#2

<details>
<summary>Build & test steps</summary>

### 1. Clone repos

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rclone/rclone.git
git clone https://github.com/rclone/go-proton-api.git
git clone https://github.com/rclone/Proton-API-Bridge.git
```

### 2. Check out fix branches

```bash
# go-proton-api: verification endpoint + Verifier types
cd /path/to/go-proton-api
git checkout fix/block-verification

# Proton-API-Bridge: block verification, retry, draft cleanup
cd /path/to/Proton-API-Bridge
git checkout fix/upload-retry

# rclone: shouldRetry fix, tests, crash fix
cd /path/to/rclone
git checkout -b fix/protondrive-backups master
git cherry-pick 0d57cb14e  # shouldRetry fix (from PR #9080)
git cherry-pick b1bd533c8  # shouldRetry tests
git cherry-pick 3c95651dc  # nil originalSize crash fix (#9117)
```

### 3. Wire up local replace directives

```bash
# In rclone/go.mod, add:
cd /path/to/rclone
go mod edit -replace github.com/rclone/go-proton-api=/path/to/go-proton-api
go mod edit -replace github.com/rclone/Proton-API-Bridge=/path/to/Proton-API-Bridge
go mod tidy

# In Proton-API-Bridge/go.mod, add:
cd /path/to/Proton-API-Bridge
go mod edit -replace github.com/rclone/go-proton-api=/path/to/go-proton-api
go mod tidy
```

### 4. Run tests

```bash
cd /path/to/rclone
go test ./backend/protondrive/...
```

### 5. Cross-compile for linux/amd64

```bash
cd /path/to/rclone
CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -v \
  --ldflags "-s -X github.com/rclone/rclone/fs.Version=v1.74.0-patched" \
  -o rclone-linux-amd64
```

### 6. Test upload

```bash
# Copy binary to target machine and test
rclone copy -vv \
  --protondrive-replace-existing-draft=true \
  --retries 5 --retries-sleep 10s \
  /path/to/file.zip YourRemote:/path/to/dest/
```

</details>

comments.author: participant21
comments.body:
First impression - the latest beta seems to work. I run rclone via a watcher script that triggers rclone sync --fast-list on local changes. Tested upload, delete, and add/remove of an empty folder - everything synced as expected (adding an empty folder is skipped by default).

Side question: my full sync takes ~7 min for ~25k files, mostly listing time. Any flags I should be using to speed this up? Currently --tpslimit 2 and --fast-list. Would bumping --tpslimit higher cause Proton rate-limit issues?

participant14
comments.body:
Thanks everyone for the fixes and tests c:

Small question because I don't know exactly how the release process works with rclone. When can we expect it to be shipped within a stable version? And to reach some depots such as Debian's one?
A few weeks? A few months? (No need for an exact date, just an idea)

I'm probably not the only one wondering, and depending on the answer, installing manually may be interesting for me 😄

Thanks :)

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
> When can we expect it to be shipped within a stable version?

If you glance at the milestones for the project you'll see that the next minor release is planned for Friday 1st May :-)

> And to reach some depots such as Debian's one?

No idea. That is out of our control.

If you check the table here https://rclone.org/install/#package-manager you can see which distros do a good job of keeping up to date and which don't.
